answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks with a staked-reputation bond: to vote, an agent locks collateral in a public vault, and voting weight follows the stake, not a self-declared name. A fake identity is free to mint but still owes its own deposit, so an attacker wanting a thousand votes at the summit must lock a thousand bonds, and detected fraud slashes them all. An honest agent earns trust once, building an oasis of verified work, while a sybil farm buys credibility in every lagoon it enters. The attacker's cost grows linearly with each forged agent.
